title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Exhibition Hall on 1968-12-21
source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat -> CD D

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1968 barn‑burner captured on a Charlie Miller soundboard – crisp despite some hiss, with standout Pigpen moments like Alligator and Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The show is celebrated for its acid‑drenched early‑Dead vibe, featuring a scorching “Alligator”, powerful Pigpen vocals on “Lovelight” and an incendiary “The Other One”. Reviewers rave about the soundboard source’s clarity and vitality after more than five decades, noting only slight tape hiss or occasional “crappy” sections that don’t detract from the overall listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers gave 4‑5 stars and praised both performance and sound quality; only a few mentioned minor tape hiss or occasional poor sound, leading to an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and vibrant Charlie Miller soundboard recording with slight tape hiss; one reviewer called it "crappy" but most note excellent clarity for a 1968 tape.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with a blazing Lovelight and rolls into an incendiary Alligator sequence, maintaining high energy throughout; short but tightly packed set that showcases Pigpen’s vocal power and the band’s early improvisational fire.

band_member_comments.Drums: The drumming is highlighted as incredible, with strong synchronization between Billy (Kreutzmann) and Mickey (Hart).
